recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless the work group separately revisits the charset-parameter guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-35811 was Published/Persuasive for the FHIR-core HTTP page. It asked to clarify wording that could imply application/fhir was a valid MIME type, with the accepted resolution to say: UTF-8 encoding SHALL be used for FHIR instances.
initial_application: Commit 4ccbcfe84ecfa7e9fffc20efa054d198c72e4df5 applied the issue to source/http.html by replacing the old sentence naming the mime type application/fhir with the current FHIR instances wording. The commit retained the separate optional MIME-parameter note without tying it to the invalid standalone media type.
additional_context: The current source/http.html Content Types and encodings section lists the formal FHIR resource MIME types as application/fhir+xml, application/fhir+json, and application/fhir+turtle immediately before the UTF-8 sentence. source/documentation.html links to http.html, confirming this page is active narrative. The originating Zulip thread confirms that the old wording was intended as a generic reference to the valid variants, and FHIR-13409 is background for optional charset/MIME-parameter guidance. Confluence searches found no FHIR-35811 record or conflicting later context.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source preserves the accepted FHIR instances wording, no longer presents application/fhir as a valid standalone MIME type, and keeps the optional MIME-parameter sentence in a context where it no longer creates the reported ambiguity.
